classification.difficultyReason: The hint directs attention to the moving hour hand. Students calculate its fractional turn during fifteen minutes and subtract that turn from the minute hand's quarter revolution.

content.prompt: What is the angle between the minute and hour hand of an analogue clock at 12:15 p.m.? Hint: Why is it less than $90^\circ$?

answer.short:
$82.5^\circ$

The hour hand has moved $7.5^\circ$ past 12.
answer.worked:
The minute hand turns through $360^\circ$ in 60 minutes; the hour hand turns through $360^\circ$ in 12 hours.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Minute-hand turn}&=\frac{15}{60}\times360^\circ\\\text{Minute-hand turn}&=90^\circ\\\text{Hour-hand turn}&=\frac{15}{12\times60}\times360^\circ\\\text{Hour-hand turn}&=7.5^\circ\\\text{Angle between hands}&=90^\circ-7.5^\circ\\\text{Angle between hands}&=82.5^\circ\end{align*}$$

The angle is less than $90^\circ$ because the hour hand has moved towards 3.
